Day Shift Motor Vehicle Theft

Bar Graph

Hotspot Map

Temporal Topology

Analysis

Daytime motor vehicle thefts in 2026 are forecasted to peak in late summer and fall, with August, October, November, and December showing both mean counts and 95% confidence intervals above the overall monthly averages. In contrast, February, January, and April are expected to have below-average thefts. Based on historical data, motor vehicle thefts are most likely to occur in downtown Washington, D.C., particularly in neighborhoods such as Downtown, Logan Circle, Shaw, and Capitol Hill, extending slightly toward Dupont Circle and Foggy Bottom. These central hotspots have been consistent across months in past years, with slightly higher intensity during the summer. Historically, daytime thefts occur most frequently in the mid-morning to early afternoon hours, especially on weekdays. Assuming these historical patterns persist, thefts in 2026 are likely to follow similar temporal and spatial trends.

Evening Shift Motor Vehicle Theft

Bar Graph

Hotspot Map

Temporal Topology

Analysis

The forecast for 2026 shows that evening motor vehicle thefts are expected to rise gradually throughout the year, reaching their highest levels in October, November, and December. Early months, such as January through March, remain below the mean count, with narrower confidence intervals, indicating more stability during winter. Spatial hotspot analysis reveals that thefts during the evening shift are most concentrated around Anacostia, Congress Heights, and along Southern Avenue SE and South Capitol Street. Another persistent hotspot appears in the Northeast quadrant, especially near Kenilworth Avenue NE and East Capitol Street NE. Smaller but notable clusters are also visible near Bloomingdale and NOMA, along Rhode Island Avenue NW and North Capitol Street. The temporal pattern shows that most thefts occur between 8:00 PM and midnight, with higher frequency toward the end of the week, especially Fridays and Saturdays.

Midnight Shift Motor Vehicle Theft

Bar Graph

Hotspot Map

Temporal Topology

Analysis

Midnight motor vehicle thefts in 2026 are forecasted to peak in December and October, with the highest 95% confidence intervals reaching 160 and 157 incidents. Overall, monthly variation is moderate, with February showing the lowest counts, falling below both the mean and the 95% confidence interval. The hotspot maps for the midnight shift show repeated concentrations of motor vehicle thefts in the central and southeastern parts of Washington, D.C. across most months in 2026. The most consistent areas of high density appear around Downtown, Shaw, and Columbia Heights, extending southeast toward Anacostia and Congress Heights. Higher counts are also visible along major roadways, including South Capitol Street, Good Hope Road SE, and Kenilworth Avenue NE, with intensity peaking in the central and eastern areas of the city. The monthly spatial pattern remains relatively stable, with noticeable hotspots present throughout the year rather than concentrated in a single season. The temporal topology shows that incidents occur more frequently between 12:00 AM and 3:00 AM, with higher activity toward the end of the week, particularly on Fridays and Saturdays. Early weekdays and later morning hours show lower activity levels. Overall, the data indicate that midnight vehicle thefts are spatially clustered in central and southeastern D.C. and temporally concentrated in the early morning hours of late week nights.
